recent_open_items.title: Allow the "-type" union hint under the strict writer options
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Fixes #831.

The `-type` record hint picks which branch of a union to write. Under
`strict=True` or `strict_allow_default=True` it was rejected instead:

    ValueError: record contains more fields than the schema specifies: -type

`write_record` builds its extras set from the record keys alone, so the hint
always landed in it. `_validation_py.py:141` already treats `-type` as
reserved rather than as data, so the writer was the side that disagreed.

Excluding it from the extras set in both `_write_py.py` and `_write.pyx`.
The reporter only hit this on `strict_allow_default`, but plain `strict`
rejects the hint the same way, so both options are covered.

The test writes a record with the hint under each option and checks the
value round-trips without it. It also keeps a genuinely unknown field in
the record to confirm that still raises, so the exemption is only the hint.

recent_open_items.title: [benchmark] Request for call-path / fairness review (GLD.SerializerBenchmark)
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Hello,

I'm Leonid Ganeline. We maintain an open multi-language serializer benchmark:

https://github.com/leo-gan/GLD.SerializerBenchmark

Your library is included in the suite (language: python, harness name: `fastavro`).
Implementation we use:

https://github.com/leo-gan/GLD.SerializerBenchmark/blob/master/python/src/benchmark/serializers/schema_avro.py

We would value a short review of whether our measurement is fair and idiomatic:

1. Does our call pattern match how you recommend using the library in performance-sensitive code?
2. Should we change options, encoder/decoder reuse, types, or buffer handling?
3. Is there a better API (or a second entry point worth a separate row in the suite)?

Concrete notes or a small PR against that wrapper would help a lot. We are happy to credit you in the docs.

The repo also includes a short Serialization course (101–401). If something important about your design is easy to misstate, a pointer is welcome—we can update the docs ourselves.

Thank

recent_open_items.title: Requesting a private channel to report a security issue (process crash / DoS)
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Hi maintainers,
I've found what I believe is a security-relevant issue in fastavro's schema parsing (a denial-of-service condition — process crash under certain execution contexts). I'd like to report it responsibly rather than posting exploit details in a public issue.
This repo doesn't appear to have a SECURITY.md or GitHub's Private Vulnerability Reporting enabled yet. Would you be willing to either:
Enable Private Vulnerability Reporting for this repo (Settings → Security → "Enable" under "Private vulnerability reporting"), which lets me submit a private, structured report directly through GitHub, or
Point me to a preferred private contact (email, etc.) for security reports?
Happy to provide a full write-up and a working PoC as soon as there's a private channel to send it through. Thanks for maintaining this project.
